findings.title: story-031's phUSD bank is unreachable when the beneficiary is the MigratorV2V3 contract: the new catch converts a safe revert-and-retry into permanent, unrecoverable reward loss
findings.description:
PhlimboV3._claimRewards:913-918 banks a failed phUSD mint into unclaimablePhUSDOf[beneficiary]. beneficiary is msg.sender, which the three call sites (stake:708, withdraw:749, claim:806) gate to `msg.sender == user || msg.sender == migrator`. So beneficiary is either the user (who can pull) or the migrator (who cannot). MigratorV2V3 exposes NO function that calls PhlimboV3.claimUnclaimablePhUSD() and has no arbitrary-call/delegatecall escape; its own claimUnclaimable(token):302 reads its OWN internal `unclaimable` mapping, a different bank. Because the phUSD was NEVER MINTED (the mint reverted), neither PhlimboV3.emergencyTransfer:361-366 nor MigratorV2V3.withdrawAll:318 can recover it — both sweep `balanceOf`, and the bank has no backing balance to sweep. unclaimablePhUSDOf is written only at :915 and drained only at :645-648 keyed by msg.sender, with no owner override or reassignment. The entitlement is therefore PERMANENTLY unrecoverable by any party.

REGRESSION-ADJACENT (the core of this finding): BEFORE story-031, during a phUSD mint-authority outage, MigratorV2V3.migrateOne:256 -> phlimboV3.stake -> _claimRewards -> phUSD.mint REVERTED, unwinding the whole iteration; migrate:204 caught it, emitted UserMigrationSkipped, and the user's V2 position was left UNTOUCHED — the owner restores authority, re-runs migration, user made whole. FULLY RECOVERABLE. AFTER story-031 the mint failure is swallowed, migrateOne COMPLETES (V2 position withdrawn and restaked into V3), the balance-delta reward measurement at :260 reads zero for the V3 component, _forward:268 forwards nothing, and the user's accrued V3 phUSD reward is stranded in unclaimablePhUSDOf[migrator] forever. Loss is bounded to the V3 auto-claim component (the V2 reward component R2 still forwards correctly), but it is permanent.

The contract's own docblock (:637-643) asserts the opposite: 'A pull that fails because authority is still missing SHOULD revert, leaving the bank intact (exactly the claimUnclaimableStable recoverability semantics).' Those recoverability semantics do NOT hold for the migrator beneficiary — a Law-2 story-faithfulness gap as well as a Law-1 value-loss one.
matchedSignatures: try phUSD.mint(beneficiary, pendingPhUSDAmount) {} catch { unclaimablePhUSDOf[beneficiary] += pendingPhUSDAmount; ... }
function claimUnclaimablePhUSD() external nonReentrant { uint256 amount = unclaimablePhUSDOf[msg.sender]; ... }
phlimboV3.stake(amount, user)  // MigratorV2V3:256 — migrator is msg.sender, therefore beneficiary
missingMitigations: MigratorV2V3 has no forwarder calling PhlimboV3.claimUnclaimablePhUSD()
emergencyTransfer/withdrawAll sweep balanceOf only — a never-minted bank has no balance to sweep
No test wires a CONTRACT migrator: test migrator is EOA address(0x5), never passed to setMigrator, so every new test exercises only the self-service path where the pull always works
triggerConditions: PhlimboV3 has lost phUSD mint authority (the exact condition story-031 exists to survive)
PhlimboV3.migrator is the MigratorV2V3 CONTRACT (the deployment intent; an EOA migrator could self-pull and would not strand)
A migrator pass runs over a user who ALREADY has a V3 position (userInfo[user].amount > 0), e.g. a user who staked directly into V3 before migration, or re-staked into V2 after pass 1

ledgerDisclosure.note: MANDATORY disclosure — this is adjacent to an owner WONT-FIX and to an open Low, and mints a NEW fingerprint that dedup will not flag. Do not auto-suppress under either precedent.

V3-M-07.relationship: V3-M-07 IS the phUSD-mint-leg finding, triaged wont-fix 2026-07-16. story-031 implemented its recommendation ('Wrap the phUSD.mint leg at :863 in the same _tryTransfer+bank pattern') ANYWAY. Its wont-fix rationale was quoted as: 'at worst a temporary, owner-reversible misconfiguration, not an external attack vector' and 'Fully recoverable (re-grant mint role or emergencyTransfer).' THE FIX INVALIDATES THAT RATIONALE ON THE MIGRATOR LEG: the banked phUSD is no longer recoverable by re-granting the mint role (nobody can call the pull) NOR by emergencyTransfer (nothing minted to sweep). The wont-fix precedent therefore does NOT automatically extend to this finding — the property it rested on no longer holds. V3-M-07 itself is now arguably moot (the leg IS wrapped); propose re-triage rather than auto-flip.
V3-M-07.action: human re-triage proposed; do NOT auto-close, do NOT reuse as suppression basis

V3-L-15.relationship: Same structural hole (migrator lacks a self-pull forwarder), but V3-L-15 is scoped to the STABLE and PROMO banks and was ranked Low on the explicit rationale: 'Value is NOT lost (owner emergencyTransfer sweeps it).' That rationale is TOKEN-SPECIFIC and does NOT extend to the phUSD bank, which holds no backing balance because the mint never happened. This finding should therefore rank ABOVE V3-L-15, not collapse into it. Fixing V3-L-15 as written (add a forwarder for claimUnclaimableStable/Promo) would NOT fix this — the forwarder must also cover claimUnclaimablePhUSD.
V3-L-15.action: do not collapse; consider widening V3-L-15's recommendation to include the phUSD pull

V3-M-05.relationship: story-031 cites V3-M-05/V3-L-14 as its motivation. V3-M-05's trigger is an EXTERNAL blocklisted recipient on the stable/promo legs — already banked by story-029. Per its own triageReason, do not conflate or collapse with the phUSD mint-authority trigger. fix-pending is human-set and never auto-closed.

findings.severityRationale: Proposed potential-medium. FOR Medium: permanent, unrecoverable value loss (C4: 'value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements'); no owner remedy exists; strictly worse than the Low-ranked V3-L-15, whose Low rests on recoverability that is absent here. AGAINST Medium (Law-3 discount, stated honestly): the trigger is an owner-controlled mint-authority revocation, and the same trigger already earned V3-M-07 a wont-fix on owner-trust grounds; assets at risk are accrued rewards, not principal. COUNTER to that discount: Law 3 exempts only OBVIOUS owner-misuse. A competent, non-malicious owner revoking mint authority (a shared-token kill-switch, per V3-M-07's own framing) would be SURPRISED that it permanently destroys migrating users' rewards with no recovery path — especially when the code's docblock promises recoverability. Surprise => footgun => in scope at honest severity. Routed for human triage rather than self-resolved.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) add a forwarder on MigratorV2V3 that calls PhlimboV3.claimUnclaimablePhUSD() (and, per V3-L-15, claimUnclaimableStable/Promo) and forwards the proceeds to the affected user; or (b) credit the phUSD bank to `user` rather than `beneficiary` when beneficiary is a contract; or (c) keep the phUSD mint leg reverting specifically on the migrator-delegated path, preserving the pre-story-031 revert-and-skip semantics that V3-M-07's wont-fix relied upon. Whichever is chosen, add a test that wires a CONTRACT migrator via setMigrator — the current suite cannot observe this class.

manualReview.title: try/catch on phUSD.mint catches out-of-gas under the 63/64 rule, so a gas-starved call could force banking on an otherwise-successful mint
manualReview.description: `try phUSD.mint(...)` forwards 63/64 of remaining gas and its catch swallows OOG as well as authorization reverts. In principle a caller who meters gas precisely could make the mint OOG, get caught, and force the amount into the bank while the outer frame survives on the retained 1/64. ASSESSED AS LIKELY SELF-LIMITING: (1) the retained 1/64 must still cover two SSTOREs, an event, the stable leg's low-level call, the promo leg, three debt-realignment SSTOREs, the principal safeTransfer and the hook — the outer tx almost certainly OOGs too and reverts atomically, leaving no state change; (2) beneficiary == msg.sender on every path, so a griefer can only force-bank their OWN reward; (3) the self-service bank is pullable, making it a no-op at worst. Recorded because confidence-of-applicability is low, not because impact is low — it composes with PATTERN-001 (if the caller is the migrator, forced banking becomes permanent loss WITHOUT any mint-authority outage, removing that finding's owner-action precondition). Warrants a Tier-3/PoC gas-metering check before dismissal.
missingMitigations: No explicit gas floor check before the try (e.g. require(gasleft() > N))
catch does not distinguish OOG from a revert reason
manualReview.routingReason: Confidence != severity. Low confidence that the pattern APPLIES (gas arithmetic likely makes it self-defeating); if it does apply, it removes PATTERN-001's owner-action precondition. Routed for a gas-metering PoC rather than dropped (Law 1).

checkedNoMatch.whyItLooksLikeAMatch: Signatures `mint(`, `IMintable`, `phUSD` all hit, and vulnerableWhen 'two paths can mint for the same accrual (double mint)' is literally true on its face: _claimRewards:913 mints, and claimUnclaimablePhUSD:649 RE-MINTS the same accrual. Any signature-driven tool would flag this.
checkedNoMatch.whyItIsNotVulnerable: The two mint paths are mutually exclusive by construction. The bank at :915 is credited ONLY inside the catch — i.e. only when the :913 mint minted nothing. The pull then re-mints exactly the banked amount and zeroes the entry (:647) before minting (CEI). Debt is realigned exactly once by the caller after _claimRewards returns (stake:715, withdraw:761, claim:808), all three of which were verified to have no early-return between the _claimRewards call and the realignment, so pending settles to zero on both branches. No accrual can be minted twice.

checkedNoMatch.whyItLooksLikeAMatch: Signatures `accPhusdPerShare`(≈accPhUSDPerShare), `rewardDebt`(≈phUSDDebt), `_updatePool` all hit; and the phlimbo-ea ledger already carries V3-M-03, the sibling bug where batchClaim aligns promoDebt BEFORE the transfer so a failed transfer destroys earned promo. The task explicitly asked whether the new code repeats that.
checkedNoMatch.whyItIsNotVulnerable: The new phUSD leg is the INVERSE of V3-M-03 and is correct. _claimRewards computes pending (:902), attempts the value leg (:913), and banks on failure (:915) — the debt is NOT touched inside _claimRewards. The caller realigns afterwards (:715/:761/:808). So a failed mint leaves the entitlement recorded in the bank, never destroyed. V3-M-03's defect is that batchClaim:503 aligns promoDebt UNCONDITIONALLY before the transfer at :506 — but batchClaim also banks at :514, so V3-M-03's live root cause is the finalizePromotion sweep, not the ordering per se. Ordering verified correct at all three call sites. V3-M-03 is untouched by this range and remains open on its own fingerprint.
checkedNoMatch.note: Also verified the rate setters settle at the OLD rate first: setDesiredAPY:270 calls _updatePool() before mutating desiredAPYBps:272 and recomputing at :273; setDepletionDuration:287 calls _updatePool() before recomputing rewardPerSecond:295. stake/withdraw call _updatePool() (:699/:746) before mutating amount and only then _updatePhUSDEmissionRate() (:725/:776). No accrual-order defect.

checkedNoMatch.verdict: REFUTED — Linear-Depletion class does NOT apply to this change
checkedNoMatch.whyItLooksLikeAMatch: Linear-Depletion is a known phlimbo-ea-origin class (V1 rate-recompute bug, recurred as phoenix-nft-staking run-18 M-01), and the task asked specifically whether story-031 touches a depletion/emission-rate recompute path.
checkedNoMatch.whyItIsNotVulnerable: The changed code touches NO rate path. claimUnclaimablePhUSD:644-651 does not call _updatePool() or _updatePhUSDEmissionRate(), and does not need to: phUSDPerSecond = (totalStaked * desiredAPYBps)/10000/SECONDS_PER_YEAR (:985) is a function of totalStaked and APY only, and the pull mutates neither. It also does not touch rewardBalance or accPhUSDPerShare. The phUSD leg is uncapped minting, not drawn from the depleting `rewardBalance` pool, so no windowEnd/runway interaction exists. The V2 discipline (no recompute inside _updatePool) is intact at :848. Rate recomputes remain confined to setDepletionDuration:295, collectReward:680, topUpPromotion:429, setPromoDepletionDuration:447, startPromotion:406 — none in the diff.
checkedNoMatch.note: totalUnclaimablePhUSD is pure bookkeeping — not consumed by any cap or solvency check. Underflow-safe at :648 because it is the sum of all per-user banks, so total >= amount always.

checkedNoMatch.whyItLooksLikeAMatch: The new code adds an external call (phUSD.mint) inside _claimRewards, and _claimRewards runs BEFORE the caller realigns phUSDDebt — a transient window where pendingPhUSD() reads stale non-zero. claimUnclaimablePhUSD also makes an external mint call.
checkedNoMatch.whyItIsNotVulnerable: CEI is respected in claimUnclaimablePhUSD: the entry is zeroed (:647) and the total decremented (:648) BEFORE the mint (:649). All state-mutating user entry points carry nonReentrant (stake:694, withdraw:739, claim:789, batchClaim:485, collectReward:669, claimUnclaimablePromo:596, claimUnclaimableStable:619, claimUnclaimablePhUSD:644). OZ v5 ReentrancyGuard is a SINGLE lock shared across all guarded functions, so the sibling set is genuinely covered — the pattern's 'per-function guards not sharing a lock' condition does not hold. The only unguarded state-mutating functions are onlyOwner setters plus pause/unpause; reentering those requires the owner (Law 3, non-malicious owner). Read-only reentrancy is moot: phUSD is a FIRST-PARTY token fixed at construction that never rotates, so the mint callee is not attacker-controlled, and the hook (an owner-set external call) fires only AFTER debt realignment (:812), outside the inconsistent window.

dbCoverageGaps.gap: vulnerability-patterns.json v1.1 has NO pattern for the failed-push-becomes-pull / pull-payment banking class, despite phlimbo-ea now carrying FOUR distinct banks (unclaimablePromoOf, unclaimableStableOf, unclaimablePhUSDOf, and MigratorV2V3.unclaimable) and the class having already produced V3-M-03, V3-L-15 and now PATTERN-001. PATTERN-001 was found by reasoning against the task-specified class list, NOT by the DB — the DB tier alone would have missed it.
proposedVulnerableWhen: banked amount is keyed to a beneficiary that has no code path to call the pull (contract beneficiary without a forwarder)
the pull re-mints/re-creates value rather than transferring custodied tokens, so no balance-sweep escape hatch can recover it
debt/entitlement aligned before the value leg so a failure destroys the entitlement (V3-M-03 shape)
catch swallows out-of-gas as well as the intended failure, allowing forced banking
banking converts a previously atomic revert-and-retry into an irreversible partial state transition
a sweep/finalize path drains the bank's backing balance
proposedNotVulnerableWhen: beneficiary is provably an EOA or a contract with a pull forwarder
entitlement recorded before/independently of the value leg
an owner escape hatch can recover the banked value
dbCoverageGaps.recommendation: Add to patterns/vulnerability-patterns.json (v1.2) with category 'staking-yield' or a new 'pull-payment' category, severity MEDIUM. Note the beneficiary-reachability check explicitly — it is the non-obvious leg.

TEST-BLIND-SPOT (not itself a finding, but material to PATTERN-001): the 5 new tests in PhlimboV3PhUSDMintBankTest declare `address migrator = address(0x5)` but NEVER call phlimbo.setMigrator(...). The address is used only as a funded ordinary staker. Every new test therefore exercises beneficiary == msg.sender == user, the one routing where the pull always succeeds. The suite is structurally incapable of observing the migrator-stranding class it introduces.
